scenario:
[LREG.5.2] The `m` flag makes `^` and `$` match at LINE boundaries. `/^b$/m` against "a\nb" matches (the second line is exactly `b`); without `m` it does not, because `^` is then the start of the text and the text starts with `a`. So this vector's answer differs by flag alone, which is the only way to observe `m` when matching is boolean.

Written because the RE2 shim got this wrong on the first attempt and nothing would have said so. RE2::Options carries a `one_line` field that reads as exactly this flag inverted, so the obvious implementation is set_one_line(!m) — and it is DEAD CODE: re2.h consults one_line only when posix_syntax is true, and posix_syntax must stay false or `\d`, `\w` and `\b` stop being classes, which is most of why DS is on RE2. set_one_line compiled, ran, and did nothing. The remedy re2.h names in the same breath is to begin the regexp with `(?m)`, which is what ds_re2_compile does. No vector covered `m` at runtime before this one — LREG.5.2's three registered fixtures all exercise `i`.

PATH PINNED: `FN_REGEX_MATCH`'s flags argument through `ds_re2_compile`'s `(?m)` prefix (libds) and `ds.re2` (Mercury). `msg` is `String?` so the match stays a beta join test: a decided match on a non-nullable slot is an alpha REGEX test with the flag folded into its pattern (RLOW.5.2.2), which never reaches that prefix and has its own vector, `RLOW.5.2.2_alpha_regex_flags`.

Expected count 2 = the Log fact plus the emitted Hit.
rules_ds:
schema Log scope logical:
    id: Int key
    msg: String? mutable

schema Hit scope logical:
    d: Int key

rule r:
    Log e where e.msg ~ /^b$/m
->
    emit Hit logical d: 0
